chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whoever fasts and forgets, and eats and drinks, should not break his fast because of his forgetting, for it is sustenance that God provided for him, so let him complete his fasting.'
ai.seo_question: Does eating or drinking due to forgetfulness break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates from Imam Ali (AS) that eating or drinking due to forgetfulness does not invalidate the fast, as the sustenance is viewed as a divine provision (rizq) granted by Allah. This ruling highlights the principle of ease in worship, distinguishing between intentional breaking and accidental consumption, a key point in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of acts performed in a state of heedlessness.
